solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: On a river, a weir capsized some ships

indicators.note: one thing set on another sits beside it, so the parts are simply placed together in a row
a boat that capsizes turns over, so the letters are turned round end to end

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the standard abbreviation for river
taken as written
a weir is a low dam across a river

explanation.surface: A boating mishap: something goes over at a weir on a river, sinking several vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the second 'a' and the weir flip over; the opening 'a' and the river stay as they are in front.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a large fleet of warships, famously the Spanish one of 1588, so it is a group of vessels.

clue.text: Element, not particularly well done, at huge cost?

blocks.note: steak that is barely cooked is rare
from the idiom 'cost the earth', meaning very expensive

explanation.surface: Sounds like a complaint about an overpriced, undercooked steak.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the loose idiom: something that costs the earth comes at huge cost. The rare earths are a real group of costly metals, so the whole clue also hints at the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare earth is one of the lanthanide group of metallic chemical elements used in magnets and electronics.

clue.text: Without principal, there’s some chaos

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase describing a state with no ruler; the answer is the noun for that state

blocks.note: first meaning: the condition of having no chief or ruler, the literal sense of the Greek original
second meaning: disorder and lawlessness

explanation.surface: A school or firm with its head away descends into mild disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greek roots are 'an' (without) and 'arkhos' (ruler), so the first part is the word's etymology; 'principal' reads like a headteacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Political disorder from lack of government, and more loosely any state of confusion or lawlessness.

clue.text: Wooden, like roof of house

definitions.note: an adjective; the answer is a noun naming a timber

indicators.note: a roof is the topmost part, and in a down entry the top is the opening letter

blocks.note: 'as' and 'like' both mean in the manner of
the first letter of the word, its top in a down entry

explanation.surface: Describing a building's wooden roof.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: ash is a tree whose timber makes wooden things.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is a common hardwood timber, so something made of it is wooden.

clue.text: Replace drink when meeting spy

indicators.note: people meeting come together side by side, so the two parts join up

blocks.note: to sup is to drink in sips
a plant is an agent placed secretly inside an organisation

explanation.surface: A spy-novel scene: swapping someone's drink at a rendezvous with an agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' here is the mole or infiltrator, not something growing.
explanation.definitionFit: To supplant is to take over the position of another, usually by scheming, which is a kind of replacing.

clue.text: Spray first of schnapps on prude

indicators.note: asks for only the opening letter of the following word

blocks.note: the opening letter of the spirit's name
a prig is a self-righteously proper person

explanation.surface: Someone squirts a strait-laced guest with schnapps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spray' is not squirting but a small bunch of flowers or leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A spray is a small stem bearing leaves or blossoms, the same thing as a small twig with foliage.

clue.text: Killjoy‘s standard mistake: unfinished musical work

indicators.note: something left unfinished lacks its ending, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: par is the standard or norm, as in golf
a typo is a typing mistake
an opera is a staged musical work

explanation.surface: A critic dismissing a half-written opera as a typical blunder by a spoilsport.
explanation.walkthrough: The opera loses its last letter before joining the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A party pooper is someone who spoils others' fun, the informal equivalent of a spoilsport.

clue.text: Go up? Not when this is the case!

definitions.text: Go up? Not when this is the case!

blocks.note: surface reading: the launch of a rocket, which is the moment it rises

blocks.clueFragment: Not when this is the case!
blocks.note: setter's reading: if the elevator is switched off, you cannot ride upstairs

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about when you can and cannot rise.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase, the answer is the moment of launch; split as a sentence, it says the elevator is out of service, which stops you going up.
explanation.definitionFit: Lift-off is the vertical take-off of a rocket, while a lift being off means an elevator not working.

clue.text: Relative being at home upset teacher periodically

indicators.note: to upset is to knock over, and in a down entry that turns the letters upside down
happening at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: someone at home is in
the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A family member is at home, sometimes upsetting a teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the even letters of the teacher, not the odd ones.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a sibling's daughter, one example of a family relation.

clue.text: Range of influence in a minister

indicators.note: one thing sitting inside another is enclosed by it

blocks.note: one's reach is the extent of one's power
'per' means a, as in five pounds per (a) head

explanation.surface: Asking how far a church minister's authority extends.
explanation.walkthrough: The small word 'a' is the outside piece: 'per' and 'a' are interchangeable in rates like 'per day'.
explanation.definitionFit: A preacher delivers sermons, and a minister of religion does exactly that.

clue.text: King holds back magical creature — it’s instinctive

definitions.note: a clause describing the thing; the answer is a noun naming it

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece goes round another
going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the letters run right to left

blocks.note: Rex is Latin for king, as in royal signatures
an elf is a small creature of folklore with magic powers

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale monarch restrains a magical being, acting on instinct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holds back' reads as one phrase meaning restrains, but splits into two signals: one for wrapping and one for turning round.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflex is an automatic, involuntary response done without thought, so it is something instinctive.

clue.text: Vehicle made from wood reportedly full of problems

indicators.note: a report is something said, so we go by sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: beech is a hardwood tree, sounding like the seaside strip
software full of faults is buggy

explanation.surface: A cart knocked together from timber that keeps breaking down.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the timber is changed by sound; the second half is taken by meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A beach buggy is a small open motor car with big tyres for driving on sand, so it is a vehicle.

clue.text: Black storage compartment holding sculpture and picture

indicators.note: something that holds another keeps it inside, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a locker is a small lockable cupboard
a bust is a sculpture of head and shoulders

explanation.surface: An inventory of a dark cupboard in a gallery containing a statue and a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picture' is a motion picture, not a painting, which the gallery surface pushes you towards.
explanation.definitionFit: A blockbuster is a hugely successful film, and picture is an informal word for a movie.

clue.text: Somewhat slovenly baker

indicators.note: 'somewhat' means only partly, so we take just a portion of the word

blocks.note: the second to fifth letters of this word

explanation.surface: A description of a rather untidy bread-maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baker' looks like a person but is the appliance that does the baking.
explanation.definitionFit: An oven is the thing that bakes food, so in crossword logic it is a baker in the sense of a device.

clue.text: Snoop around back of slate quarry

indicators.note: going around something encloses it, so one piece surrounds the other
the back is the end, so only the closing letter is wanted

blocks.note: to pry is to snoop into others' business
the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone nosing around behind a slate quarry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarry' is not a pit for stone but a hunted animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarry and prey both mean an animal being hunted or chased by a predator.

clue.text: Room for eg Hoover that’s not working in alcove I redesigned?

indicators.note: a redesigned thing is rebuilt to a new plan, so the letters take a new order
one thing in another is enclosed by it

blocks.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange
a machine that is off is not working

explanation.surface: A broken vacuum cleaner stored in a redone nook: where do you keep the Hoover?
explanation.walkthrough: Hoover is not the vacuum cleaner but Herbert Hoover, the 31st US president; the rearranged letters split around the 'not working' piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oval Office is the US president's working room in the White House, used by every president including Hoover.

clue.text: Show with Brontë heroine on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard, not seen, so we go by sound

blocks.note: Jane Eyre is the heroine of Charlotte Brontë's novel

explanation.surface: A radio programme featuring a Brontë heroine, such as a Jane Eyre adaptation.
explanation.walkthrough: The heroine's surname gives the sound; the spelling changes to the word for display.
explanation.definitionFit: To air something is to show it publicly or broadcast it, as when a programme is aired.

clue.text: Complained couple has no time for urgent advice

indicators.note: having none of something means it is removed from the word

blocks.note: to carp is to complain pettily
a romantic couple is called an item
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A grumbling pair with no time spare gives some pressing tips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couple' is the informal 'item', not 'pair' or 'two'; the time letter comes out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpe diem is Latin for 'seize the day', a motto urging people to act now rather than wait.

clue.text: Psychiatrist stole package

blocks.note: shrink is slang for a psychiatrist
a stole is a shawl or wrap worn over the shoulders

explanation.surface: A news item: a psychiatrist pinched a parcel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole' is not the past tense of steal but a scarf.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrinkwrap is to package goods in tight plastic film, so it is a way of packaging.

clue.text: Bury with one manager, initially caretaker

indicators.note: 'initially' means at the start, so only the opening letter is used

blocks.note: to inter is to bury a body
the Roman numeral for one
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A football club buries its troubles under a stand-in manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caretaker' is the adjective used in sport for a temporary manager.
explanation.definitionFit: An interim or caretaker appointment is a temporary one, held until a permanent person takes over.

clue.text: Award at first given to partner’s hairstyle?

indicators.note: 'at first' points at the start, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
'to' and 'fro' are partners in the phrase 'to and fro'

explanation.surface: A prize handed to someone's spouse for their hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partner' reads as a spouse, but it is the word that pairs with 'to' in a fixed phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An Afro is a rounded, bushy style of naturally curly hair.

clue.text: Car driving aid that’s being investigated?

definitions.note: a relative clause describing someone; the answer is a noun naming them

blocks.note: Audi is a German car make
a golfer drives the ball off a tee

explanation.surface: A gadget that helps you drive a car turns out to be under investigation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driving' is golf, not motoring: the tee is what a golfer drives from.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditee is the person or organisation whose accounts are examined by an auditor.

clue.text: Turning valves produced liquid

indicators.note: turning round makes the word face the other way, so its letters run backwards

blocks.note: taps are valves controlling a flow of water

explanation.surface: Plumbing: opening the valves lets the liquid out.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a coy way of saying someone expelled saliva.
explanation.definitionFit: Spat is the past tense of spit, to eject saliva from the mouth, which is producing liquid.

clue.text: Artwork made by a couple of Greek characters

blocks.note: pi is the sixteenth letter of the Greek alphabet
eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A piece of art created by two people from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' are letters of the alphabet, not people.
explanation.definitionFit: A pietà is a painting or sculpture of the Virgin Mary holding the dead Christ, most famously by Michelangelo.

clue.text: Complete brigade moved into a French stronghold at last

indicators.note: things that are moved are shifted about, so the letters change places
going into something places one piece inside another
'at last' means at the very end, so only the closing letter is kept

blocks.note: un is French for a
taken as written, as the letters to rearrange
the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A whole military unit relocates into a French fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged unit sits between the French article and the last letter of the stronghold.
explanation.definitionFit: An unabridged text is the full version with nothing cut, so it is complete.

clue.text: Allowed to remove cap that’s dreadful

indicators.note: taking off a cap removes the top, and in a down entry that is the opening letter

blocks.note: something lawful is allowed by law

explanation.surface: Someone is permitted to take off a hideous hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cap' reads as headgear but means the top letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Awful and dreadful are synonyms meaning very bad or unpleasant.

clue.text: Tribune rudely ignoring new city

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so a letter is dropped
done rudely is done roughly, so the letters are knocked about

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A newspaper called the Tribune rudely snubs a newly built town.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the new letter out of the newspaper name first, then rearrange the remaining six.
explanation.definitionFit: Beirut is the capital and largest city of Lebanon.

clue.text: Perhaps Douglas gets conservative care, initially

blocks.note: the Douglas fir is a kind of tree
staid means conservative and unadventurous

explanation.surface: A man called Douglas receives cautious medical treatment at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' is part of the definition, not a signal to take first letters; Douglas is a tree, with 'Perhaps' marking it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: First aid is the immediate treatment given to an injured person before full medical help, so it is the earliest care.

clue.text: Free fairground attraction ejects last in line

indicators.note: to eject is to throw out, so a letter is removed
the last one in is at the very end, so only the closing letter is meant

blocks.note: a fairground ride such as a carousel
the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A free fairground ride throws out whoever is at the back of the queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last in line' reads as the end of a queue but means the closing letter of the word 'line'.
explanation.definitionFit: To rid is to free someone or something of an unwanted thing, as in 'rid the house of mice'.

clue.text: Graduate left lesson in castle

blocks.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree holder
L is the abbreviation for left
the moral of a story is its lesson

explanation.surface: A graduate abandoned a class held inside a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is the link to the definition here, not a container signal; Balmoral is the royal family's castle in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Balmoral Castle in Aberdeenshire is the British monarch's private Scottish residence.

clue.text: Read novel — gosh, it’s enchanting!

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange
'my!' is an exclamation of surprise like 'gosh!'

explanation.surface: A reader gushes over a delightful book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like the book but signals rearrangement; 'gosh' is a mild exclamation like 'my!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamy means delightful and wonderful, as if from a dream, which is close to enchanting.
